paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of and by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” of two probing methods—mBERT-targ and XLM-targ (light and dark blue, respectively)—and two permutation baselines—mBERT-permute and XLM-permute (light and dark green, respectively)—across nine language families or categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 40 with major tick marks at intervals of 10, and error bars indicate standard deviation for each bar. Within each language family group, the four bars are arranged in the same order as the legend: mBERT-targ (light blue), XLM-targ (dark blue), mBERT-permute (light green), and XLM-permute (dark green). The effect values vary across families: for example, in IE-Baltic, mBERT-targ reaches approximately 22, XLM-targ is around 15, and both permute baselines are near 5–6; in Isolate, mBERT-targ peaks at about 35, XLM-targ at 25, while permute baselines drop to near 2; in Uralic, mBERT-targ is around 28, XLM-targ around 21, and permute baselines are near 1–2. Most target models (mBERT-targ and XLM-targ) show higher effect values than their permuted counterparts, with Isolate and Uralic exhibiting the highest target effects and the lowest permuted effects. The bars are not sorted by magnitude, but rather grouped by language family along the horizontal axis, which is categorical and unordered. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color-coded grouping.
